The `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class is responsible for printing the help message with specified formatting. The method takes various parameters such as the PrintWriter, width, command line syntax, header, options, left padding, description padding, and footer.

Next, I will perform a step-by-step diagnosis to localize the fault.
# Diagnosis

## 1. Understanding the Issue
The current bug report describes an infinite loop in the wrapping code of the `HelpFormatter` class. It mentions that when there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, the `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop until the JVM crashes with an OutOfMemoryError. The reported test case involves setting the width to 20 and printing the help message, leading to a hang and crash.

## 2. Analyzing the Failing Test
The failing test `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored` sets up `Options` with a long description, creates a `HelpFormatter`, and then attempts to print help with a specified width. This test does not directly match the reported test case but involves a similar aspect of printing help messages.

## 3. Investigating the `HelpFormatter#printHelp` Method
The `HelpFormatter#printHelp` method is responsible for formatting and printing the help message. It takes the provided width into account while formatting the output to fit within the specified constraints.

## 4. Potential Root Cause
Given the reported issue of the `HelpFormatter` going into an infinite loop when there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, it is likely that there is a problem with how the `HelpFormatter` handles long descriptions or word wrapping. The test `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored` may indirectly trigger this behavior by setting the width in a way that exposes this issue.

## 5. Conclusion
The root cause of the infinite loop in the `HelpFormatter` seems to be related to word wrapping or handling of long descriptions in the `printHelp` method. Further investigation into how the `HelpFormatter` handles long lines and word wrapping is needed to pinpoint the exact cause of the infinite loop.

Next, I will suggest the best locations to be fixed based on this diagnosis.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
